strings.name: Travis Kalanick
strings.summary: Kalanick moved from file-sharing startups to cofounding Uber with Garrett Camp and expanding it globally. Ride-hailing changed urban services while raising labor, regulatory and safety disputes. In 2017 he resigned as CEO under investor pressure after workplace-culture and harassment investigations. He later developed City Storage Systems and CloudKitchens, unveiling Atoms in 2026 for food, transport and industrial robotics.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 16 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Cofounded Uber and expanded ride-hailing platforms, changing urban mobility and debates over digital-labor governance.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Studied computer engineering at UCLA, leaving in 1998 without that degree to pursue startups.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Expanding ride-hailing
strings.highlights.h1.text: Developed Uber with partners and brought smartphone-based rides to many countries and cities.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Technology for physical industries
strings.highlights.h2.text: Expanded from shared kitchens into food automation and specialized robotics.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Unveiled Atoms
strings.timeline.t1.text: Publicly rebranded City Storage Systems and described food, mining and transport technologies.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Developed City Storage Systems
strings.timeline.t2.text: After Uber management, built shared-kitchen and related food-infrastructure businesses.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Resigned as Uber CEO
strings.timeline.t3.text: Left under investor pressure after a workplace review prompted by harassment and discrimination complaints.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Uber launched; became CEO
strings.timeline.t4.text: San Francisco rides went live, and he became CEO that year before expanding the platform.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Cofounded Uber
strings.timeline.t5.text: Joined Garrett Camp and other partners in establishing the smartphone ride-hailing company.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Red Swoosh acquired
strings.timeline.t6.text: Akamai acquired the content-delivery business he had helped build, ending that venture’s independent operation.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Cofounded Red Swoosh
strings.timeline.t7.text: Developed peer-to-peer content distribution with engineering partners, continuing file-transfer entrepreneurship.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Left UCLA for Scour
strings.timeline.t8.text: Left computer-engineering studies to work on search and peer-to-peer file-sharing services.
